seoTitle: How to Verify Your Shopify Account Step by Step
metaDescription: Confused about verifying your Shopify account? Here's a step-by-step walkthrough of Shopify's identity verification process and what it unlocks.
intro: Verifying your Shopify account is one of the first hurdles new store owners run into, and skipping it can quietly block access to features needed later, like accepting real payments. It isn't a single button labeled "Verify" so much as a handful of confirmations scattered across the admin and account settings, which is exactly why so many people think they're done when they're not. This guide walks through where those confirmations live, what the dashboard looks like before and after handling them, and what Shopify's own identity verification process asks for. Along the way it covers the small details, like which inbox Shopify emails and what a failed identity check usually means, that cause most of the "why isn't this working" confusion. It's written for anyone setting up a new Shopify store who wants to avoid discovering a blocked feature mid-launch.
prerequisites: A valid government-issued photo ID (passport, driver's license, or national ID card) and a device with a working camera, in case Shopify's identity verification step is triggered

steps.heading: Log into your Shopify admin
steps.body: Everything about verification starts from your store's admin, reached at your unique myshopify.com address or a connected custom domain. Once signed in, Shopify treats the login itself as the first layer of identity confirmation, tying every action back to the account and email registered. If you manage more than one store, note which one you're working in before you start: account-level settings like verification apply per account, not per store, and it's easy to check the wrong store's status. Bookmark the correct admin URL once you find it, since jumping between stores through search results is a common way to lose track of which one is being configured.

steps.heading: Check your account status from the dashboard
steps.body: The home screen greets you with "You've got a product to sell" and two prompt cards side by side: one to choose a store design, the other to set up payments. That payments card is the clearest visual cue that verification-related setup is still outstanding, since Shopify won't let real transactions flow until a payment provider is activated and any required identity check is confirmed. A banner in the lower-left corner also tracks the trial countdown, a separate clock from verification but worth noting so the two aren't confused; running out the trial without ever touching the payments card is a common way stores launch with no way to get paid. Treat that card as a to-do item, not background decoration.

image.caption: The Shopify admin home right after setup, with prompts to choose a theme and set up payments still showing — the payments card is where identity and business verification happen.

steps.heading: Open the account switcher to confirm your details
steps.body: Click the store name or avatar in the top-right corner and a panel drops down listing every store tied to the login, plus a separate "My Store Admin" entry showing the email address the account is registered to. This is worth checking early, because Shopify sends verification-related confirmations to that exact address, and a typo or an old inbox here is one of the most common reasons people think verification is stuck when it's really just an email that never arrived. The same panel is where to log out, switch between a personal and a business store, or jump to the Help Center. Running multiple stores under one login also makes mismatched verification status obvious here: one store can be fully verified while a newer one still needs the same steps repeated.

image.caption: The account switcher, showing every store tied to the login and the exact email address Shopify uses to send verification and account confirmations.

steps.heading: See what verification unlocks in the editor
steps.body: Once the account details check out, head into the Online Store editor to see the practical payoff. Verified accounts get full access to the theme customizer: editing sections like the homepage banner, adjusting the header, and adding blocks to any template without Shopify holding features back pending confirmation. This is also where the gap between a browsing account and a working store becomes obvious. A live-looking storefront can be previewed and built out freely, but nothing customers see is sellable until the payments and identity details behind it are confirmed. It's a useful gut check: if the storefront edits freely but checkout still refuses real cards, the payments and identity side of verification is what's unfinished, not the storefront side.

image.caption: The theme editor for a store's homepage, fully accessible once the account is confirmed — this level of customization is one of the features unverified accounts get prompted to unlock first.

steps.heading: Complete payments setup and identity verification
steps.body: Click through the "Set up payments" card and Shopify asks for the business or personal details needed to activate Shopify Payments: legal name, address, and banking information. Separately from that, Shopify may ask for identity verification, a distinct step it can trigger when setting up or updating Shopify Payments, when applying for Shopify Capital or Credit, when signing up for certain plans, or if it flags suspicious account activity. When it's asked for, Shopify's own documentation is specific about what's needed: a government-issued photo ID with all four corners visible (both sides, if the ID has them), photographed in good lighting, plus a short liveness check using the device's camera, essentially a live selfie, not an uploaded photo. Have the physical ID and a working camera ready before starting, and make sure the legal name and address entered match bank or government records exactly. A mismatch is the most common reason this step gets kicked back for manual review instead of approved right away.

steps.heading: Watch for confirmation, then keep an eye on it going forward
steps.body:
Shopify typically reviews submitted details within a short window and either confirms instantly or emails for more information; identity verification can take a few minutes but longer if manual review is needed. Check both the bell icon in the admin and the inbox confirmed earlier, since some notices only appear in one place. Respond promptly to any request for more documentation. An incomplete verification can pause payouts even after the store is otherwise live and taking orders.

Verification is not always a one-time event, either. Adding a new payment method, changing the business address, expanding into a new country, applying for Shopify Capital, or Shopify detecting unusual activity on the account can all trigger a fresh identity check. Get in the habit of glancing at account settings and dashboard prompts after any major change, so a new verification request is caught before it holds up an order, not after a customer is already asking where their payment went.

troubleshooting.problem: The liveness check or selfie keeps getting rejected
troubleshooting.cause: Shopify's identity verification needs good lighting, a steady camera, and an unobstructed face; a dim room, glare, or something covering part of the face is enough to fail it.
troubleshooting.fix: Retry somewhere with even, bright lighting, remove glasses or hats, hold the device steady, and follow the on-screen framing guide until the check completes.

troubleshooting.problem: The ID photo won't go through, or verification sits stuck in review
troubleshooting.cause: The photo doesn't show all four corners of the document, is blurry, or is missing the reverse side on an ID that has one.
troubleshooting.fix: Re-photograph the full document in good lighting, capturing both sides if it has them, then resubmit.

troubleshooting.problem: A verification request shows up again after the store was already verified
troubleshooting.cause: Identity verification isn't a one-time gate. Shopify can re-trigger it for a new payment method, a changed business address, a Capital or Credit application, or flagged account activity.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the specific prompt in the admin or email to see which trigger applies, then complete that verification flow instead of assuming it's an error.

faq.question: Why does Shopify require account verification?
faq.answer: Shopify's stated reasons are compliance with financial regulations and protecting the platform from impersonation, account takeovers, and fraud, alongside confirming a store is run by a legitimate business before enabling features like Shopify Payments.

faq.question: What exactly does Shopify's identity verification ask for?
faq.answer: A valid government-issued photo ID, such as a passport, driver's license, or national ID card, photographed with all four corners visible, plus a short liveness check through the device's camera. It's more than the vague "sometimes a government ID" many guides mention.

faq.question: What triggers identity verification, besides setting up payments?
faq.answer: Shopify can also request it when applying for Shopify Capital or Credit, when signing up for certain plans, if it detects suspicious account activity, or when recovering account access after losing two-step authentication or email access.

faq.question: What happens if I skip verification?
faq.answer: The storefront can still be browsed and customized, but real payments can't be accepted until the identity and business details behind Shopify Payments are confirmed.

faq.question: How long does Shopify account verification take?
faq.answer: Often just a few minutes if the submitted details match, but it can take longer if Shopify requests additional documentation. Watch both the email on file and the admin notification bell.

faq.question: Where do I check if my account is verified?
faq.answer: The dashboard's "Set up payments" prompt disappearing is the clearest sign. Settings > Payments in the admin shows the current status directly.

verifiedNote: The dashboard, account switcher, and editor screens come from a recording. The verification requirements and triggers were re-checked against Shopify's official identity verification documentation in September 2026, which corrected the original draft's vague "sometimes a government ID" line: Shopify's process specifically requires a photo ID with all corners visible plus a live camera-based liveness check, and it can trigger for reasons beyond setting up payments, including Capital or Credit applications, plan sign-ups, suspicious activity, and account recovery.
